protocol.question: Can a function-preserving shift between LN2 and the last MLP input bias decrease teacher agreement when the public base replaces B?
protocol.mechanism: For parent A and a, add v to LN2 bias and subtract A v from a. The native preactivations agree for all inputs in real arithmetic. In half-average with public weights the shift is (A0-A)v/4, also with A permuted by the fixed author assignment. B and its bias are replaced by public values after each source assembly.
protocol.construction: One fixed MNIST parent, 800 cached synthetic views, no partner or real inputs. Optimize the mean positive teacher-class margin of public B replacement in two contexts with standard LBFGS, 20 iterations, library max_eval 30 (line search can exceed it). The squared sum of LN2 bias and input bias changes relative to their parent norms is <=1. One final FP32 pair.
protocol.gate: All native teacher decisions retained, no increase in ordinary public TA or fixed public AGA agreement, decrease in both B-replacement contexts. Source gate alone does not authorize a robustness claim. Record a public canonicalization by setting the published LN2 bias to the public value and adding A(beta_published-beta_public) to the incoming bias.
protocol.budget: No end-to-end image forwards, new synthetic images, defense expert updates, full evaluation or new attack runs in this source test.
protocol.scope: Standard affine reparameterization used as an exact native-function control. Only the public-base proxies and this fixed budget are examined. Canonicalization uses the published pair and public LN2 bias.
